newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks' GDR issue plans delayed to 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks' GDR issue plans delayed to 1997.

text.p: Plans by Korea Long-Term Credit Bank and Boram Bank to issue a combined $270 million worth of global depositary receipts abroad have been delayed until next year, the finance ministry said on Monday.
It said in a statement that the ailing Seoul stock market was behind the delay.
"Local banks have been experiencing difficulty going ahead with their issue plans because of the (ailing) local stock market," the statement said.
Korea Long-Term Credit Bank originally planned to issue $200 million worth of receipts this year, but requested to delay the issue until the second quarter of 1997, the statement said.
Boram's plan to issue $70 million has also been postponed until February next year, it said.
The Seoul stock market has been languishing due to slowing corporate earnings in line with dwindling exports and fears of share oversupply.
The composite stock index fell 3.94 points on Monday to close at 692.17, the lowest level since September 18, 1993, when it ended at 685.94.
Last month Cho Hung Bank issued $180 million worth of depositary receipts at a premium of 1.0 percent.
It was far below the 28 percent premium on Kookmin Bank's $300 million depositary receipt issue early this year, the ministry statement said.
